faq.title: Answers before you upload.
faq.intro: Clear boundaries for mortgage, discovery, and tax-form PDF extraction.
faq.a1: onepagers is a set of focused PDF extraction tools. Each one is built for a specific document family and keeps extracted facts connected to their source.
faq.a2: The current tools cover Closing Disclosure and Loan Estimate PDFs, legal discovery productions, and K-1 or 1099 tax forms.
faq.q3: What does the Closing Doc Extractor do?
faq.a3: It finds loan amount, interest rate, monthly principal and interest, closing costs, cash to close, term, and lender name in supported mortgage disclosure PDFs.
faq.q4: What does the Discovery Doc Extractor do?
faq.a4: It builds a first-pass index of dates, parties, dollar amounts, exhibits, and Bates references, with the source file and page beside each result.
faq.q5: What does the K-1 Extractor do?
faq.a5: It recognizes supported K-1 and 1099 layouts, maps their labeled box values, and shows the source box, page, confidence, and text used for each field.
faq.a6: The tools differ. Discovery can use OCR on pages without usable text; the mortgage and tax extractors require a selectable text layer, so run OCR before uploading an image-only PDF to those tools.
faq.q7: Can I see where an extracted value came from?
faq.a7: Yes. Depending on the tool, results include the source file, page, form box, Bates reference, nearby text, or a highlighted source region.
faq.a8: They describe how strongly the extractor matched a value to its expected label, box, or source text. Use them to prioritize review, not as a guarantee.
faq.q9: Can I correct an extracted value?
faq.a9: The K-1 Extractor lets you edit values in its review table and export the checked rows. The other tools provide their own result exports without an in-page correction table.
faq.q10: What file types does onepagers accept?
faq.a10: The upload controls accept PDF files. They do not accept Word documents, images, spreadsheets, or other file types directly.
faq.q11: How large can my PDF be?
faq.a11: Free processing is capped at 8 MB and 15 pages across the tools. Discovery accepts batches up to 50 PDFs and one PDF up to 80 pages; K-1 allows up to 25 pages, while the mortgage extractor uses its free 15-page boundary.
faq.q12: How many PDFs can I upload at once?
faq.a12: Discovery accepts up to 50 PDFs in one batch. Closing and K-1 handle one PDF per review.
faq.q13: What happens when a file is too large or too long?
faq.a13: Files over a free-processing boundary are accepted and queued for heavy processing where that tool supports it. Discovery rejects more than 50 PDFs or a PDF over 80 pages, and K-1 rejects PDFs over 25 pages.
faq.q14: Are my documents stored after processing?
faq.a14: Uploaded PDF bytes are deleted after processing. The active review keeps extracted results and source metadata for the current session; the tools do not provide a document history.
faq.q15: Does onepagers train on my documents?
faq.a15: No. The current product copy states that uploaded documents are not used to train models and processed file contents are not made available to staff.
faq.a16: The public experience is the browser upload tool. A public, documented API with developer signup and API keys is not advertised in this version.
faq.a17: Accuracy depends on the document layout, text layer, scan quality, and how closely the PDF matches a supported form. Review important values against the source document.
faq.a18: The browser tools are available to try under their free-processing limits. No paid-processing price or payment flow is published yet.
faq.a19: Yes. Depending on the tool, you can download CSV or JSON results, or a checked CSV from the K-1 review screen.
faq.a20: They are for people who repeatedly review mortgage disclosures, legal discovery productions, or tax forms and need structured facts without losing the source evidence.
